Some links on this page are affiliate links. Affiliate disclosure.

Ten of the 13 tools this guide covers have an official iPhone app in the US App Store today, and eight have an official Android listing on Google Play. Kling AI, Runway, Dreamina, Grok, Google Flow, Google Gemini, and Meta AI are on both stores; Pika and Krea are iPhone only; and we found no app published by Higgsfield or Wan. Store listings and vendor pages were read Nov 17, 2026, 9:49–9:57 AM ET (6:49–6:57 AM PT). In-app prices are copied from the App Store’s own list, and anything a listing does not state is marked unknown. If you only want the lowest price per second, see the cheapest AI video generator by model.

Key takeaways

  • On both stores. Kling AI, Runway, Dreamina, Grok, Google Flow, Google Gemini, and Meta AI.
  • iPhone only. Pika and Krea. Luma Dream Machine is confirmed on iPhone only. Hailuo is confirmed on Android; its iPhone link returned not found in the US store on Nov 17, 2026.
  • No vendor app found. Higgsfield and Wan. Both stores return apps from other developers under those names, so check the developer name.

Which AI video generators have an official app?

Of the 13 tools this guide covers, ten have an official iPhone app in the US App Store today and eight have an official Android listing on Google Play. Kling AI, Runway, Dreamina, Grok, Google Flow, Google Gemini, and Meta AI are on both stores. Pika and Krea are on iPhone only, and Luma is confirmed on iPhone only. Hailuo is confirmed on Android; the iPhone listing its own site points to returned not found in the US store on Nov 17, 2026. We found no app published by Higgsfield or Wan on either store. Searches on both stores also return apps from other developers under these names, so check the developer name before you install or pay.

How did we check, and what counts as official?

An app counts as official here when the seller or developer name on the store listing is the vendor’s own, or when the vendor’s own site links to that listing. Each iPhone listing was read from the US App Store, including its seller, rating, and in-app purchase list. Each Android listing was read from Google Play in the US, including its developer name, rating, and whether it is marked with in-app purchases. Store listings do not state the resolution or audio of what a purchase buys, so those are marked not stated. Per-second costs come from the vendor’s web pricing page or from our catalog, never from a store listing.

What do the apps charge in-app?

The App Store lists up to ten in-app items per app, with a name and a US price, and it does not state the billing period unless the period is in the item name. Runway’s Standard is $14.99 a month in the app and $15 on the web. Kling’s Standard plan (monthly) is $10.00 in the app, which matches the web list price; the web page read Nov 14, 2026 PT showed $8.80 a month after a $6.99 first month. Pika’s 1,500-credit pack is $34.99 in the App Store, about $0.0233 per credit; on the web, packs are 60 credits per $1, about $0.0167 per credit.

    What does a second of video cost on each app’s plan?

    It depends on the plan and the model, and four of these apps do not publish enough to work it out. Where the vendor publishes credits per clip, the plan figures are: $0.025 per second for Veo 3.1 Lite at 720p on Google AI Pro in Google Flow; $0.0333 per second for Pika H3 Flex at 768p on Pika Starter; $0.06 per second for Luma Ray3.2 at 720p on Luma Plus; and $0.144 per second for Gen-4 Turbo on Runway Standard. Each assumes you use every credit you pay for, and audio is not stated on any of those rows. Kling, Grok, Dreamina, and Hailuo do not publish credits per clip for their plans on the pages we read, so their in-app cost per second is unknown.

    How do you tell an official app from a look-alike?

    Check the seller or developer name on the listing, and prefer the link on the vendor’s own website. On Nov 17, 2026, Google Play search for Pika and for Higgsfield returned listings from other developers under those names. A Google Play listing with the title “Luma Dream Machine” is published by a different developer from Luma’s iPhone app (the listing names Infinity AI Solutions). A matching name and logo are not proof that a listing is official. If a listing is marked “Contains ads,” or the developer name is not the vendor’s, we treat it as unconfirmed.

    What is confirmed, and what is not?

    Unknown, and not guessed: whether Hailuo’s iPhone app is available in the US App Store; whether the Google Play listing titled “Luma Dream Machine,” published by a different developer, is official; whether Higgsfield or Wan publish an app under another name; the billing period of App Store items whose name does not state it; the credits, resolution, and audio attached to any in-app purchase, which store listings do not state; credits per clip on Kling, Grok, Dreamina, and Hailuo plans; and Meta AI’s video generation limits. Store ratings and prices are for the US stores and change over time.

    How do we calculate this?

    Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page (https://vidfare.com/about/).
